body: claimed: mkinney (Claude agent, M5) · 2026-11-10 02:29 UTC · plan: research - answer the four design questions (representation of a carried field, floors, clipping, an agreement lane) in a comment before any code

Design research (agent, M5), working from `carry.rs`'s laws: re-index, never re-sample; two sides; the floor judged once it has faced a tool.

### 1. Representation: a transformed query frame, not a re-sample
A signed distance field is **invariant under rigid motion**: the distance from `p` to the carried solid is the distance from `T⁻¹p` to the original solid. So a carried field is the **same field** (shell, analytic box (#633), cut layers) plus a rigid transform `T`, evaluated as `field.distance(T⁻¹ p)`.
- **Exactness:** nothing is re-sampled and nothing is lost. That's the field analogue of "re-index, never re-sample", and it's exact for any rigid `T`.
- **Phase 1 keeps `carry.rs`'s scope:** the 8 signed permutations that keep Z on ±Z (`LatticeTurn`). Under those, a vertical column in the new frame maps to a vertical column, possibly reversed, in the field's own frame. So the verdict march (`march.rs`: shell parity along a vertical ray, then a root-find) stays exact with a sign flip in Z. Every other turn keeps `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL` by name.
- **Later:** general rotations are possible for a field, which the lattice can't do. They need ray parity along an arbitrary direction (`column_crossings` generalised). That's a follow-up, not phase 1.

### 2. Floors: the lowest solid crossing, read by a march from below
The field holds a closed solid, so there's no separate floor array. A column's floor is its **lowest solid crossing**, found by the same march run upward (a `march_up` twin).
- **After a flip:** the former top comes out naturally as the solid's lower surface.
- **Cut through:** a column the tool went right through has **no** crossing and reads air on both sides. That's the column law's "cut through stays cut through", for free.
- **Judging the floor once it has faced a tool:** keep the column body's flag on the carried body. When it's set, the verdict also runs the upward march against the part's bottom.

### 3. Clipping to a later setup's stock: CSG intersection
`stock_sim_carry`'s clip loop (`dex.lower(i, t)`) becomes an **intersection** with the new setup's stock: `d = max(d_body, d_stock)`. With #633's closed-form box that's an O(1) term per query. A `clip: Option<AnalyticBox>` (or a field) on the carried body is evaluated in `mag_at`/`distance`'s max, the same way the cut layer already lifts the mesh term.

### 4. Equivalence: an agreement lane
A heavy-lane `carry_engine_agreement`, in the shape of `stock_engine_agreement`, runs the carried-stock fixtures (`setup_carry`, `rest_across_setups`, `carried_verify`, covering flips and quarter turns) on **both** bodies. It requires **0 findings** within `FIELD_VERDICT_EPS` on the rest and gouge verdicts, top and floor.

### Proposed build order (each step behaviour-neutral until the switch)
- **(A)** `SdfField` gains a query transform (`Rigid8`) plus invariance tests: distance at `Tp` after the carry equals distance at `p` before.
- **(B)** `march_up` and a two-sided verdict on a field.
- **(C)** The clip term (intersection).
- **(D)** `carry::Body` becomes an enum `{Column, Field}` behind the same API, plus the agreement lane (A–C exercised on real fixtures).
- **(E)** The app holders (#586) move onto `Stock` / the body enum, with the column engine still the default. #589 then flips the default.

I'll start on **(A)**. Each step is its own small PR referencing #637.

**Step A done** (branch issue/637-carried-field-a, gating): `CarriedField` plus `LatticeTurn::unapply`/`then`. Through all 8 turns and their compositions, the carried field reads **bit-identical**, cut layers included.

**Design finding for step B** (`march_up`): it isn't a mechanical twin of `march`.
- **What the down-march relies on:** its exactness rests on `cut_ups` (`field_ray`), a per-cell record of where a **downward** vertical ray first meets the solid. It's a conservative lower bound that lets flanks and grooves answer at their own geometry.
- **Why that matters here:** under a Z-flip, a carried column's **top** in the new frame is the original's **floor**, so reading it is an **upward** march in the field's own frame. An upward march needs the mirror companion (an upward ray's entry, an upper bound) for the same exactness. Without it, it can only bracket at the cell boundary where the stored sign flips. That's exact on the mesh's planes, but loose (by up to a cell) on a cut's tilted flank seen from below.
- **Options for B:**
  1. **Add `cut_downs`:** maintained by the same claim law in `field_cut` at the same cost class. Exact both ways.
  2. **Restrict an upward read to uncut floors:** after a flip, the former bottom is uncut stock, which is exactly the mesh planes. Refuse by name a column whose lower surface carries a cut. That's safe and smaller, and covers every re-clamp where the earlier setup didn't cut through from below.
- **Recommendation:** (2) first. It's the column body's own common case (a part flipped onto a machined top face) and exact. Then (1) only if a fixture needs a cut read from below.

I'll proceed with step A's PR, then B as option (2).

Status: steps A-D are up: #646 (A) and #649 (B) are labelled `merge-ready`, #651 (C) is labelled `merge-ready` and #656 (D, the read-back plus the `carry_engine_agreement` lane) is in review. Step E moves the app holders onto this path. It is #586's work, which sits on #642 (stacked on #595), so it waits for those to merge rather than stacking on two parents at once.

claimed: issue-worker-max (Fable 5.1) · 2026-11-11 04:28 UTC · worktree/branch issue/637-carried-stock-field (fork synced at v0.16.0, branched from upstream/main) · plan: step E design - answer the holder/mutation-path questions (simulate(&mut body.dex), lower, Held, dex_mut) with evidence from carry.rs, field_body.rs and the app holders, record the decision, then implement what fits one PR or file the slices

Design, step E (agent, issue-worker-max, on upstream/main 5fd45923 with #646/#649/#651/#656 merged). Steps A-D settled the **read**; what is left is the **mutation path** and the holders. Evidence from the code, then one recommendation.

## 1. Representation: the view stands, and it is exact for the verdicts

- `CarriedField` (`field_carry.rs`) is the same `SdfField` seen through `LatticeTurn::unapply`: `distance(p) = field.distance(turn.unapply(p))`, then `max` with the clip block. A signed distance is invariant under rigid motion, so no value is re-sampled; `field_carry` (8 tests) pins the read bit-identical through all 8 turns and their compositions, cut layers included.
- Under a lattice turn a vertical column of the new frame is a vertical column (perhaps reversed) of the field's own, so the verdict reads are one down-march each (`field_body::read_column`): `march` for the top, `floor_at` for the floor, swapped on a flip. The read-back (`column_body`) lands on the SAME `carry::Body`, so `deviate` (two-sided), `display`, `volume`, `bounds` are the column carry's own code: `carry_engine_agreement` holds tops and floors to 1e-6 per column and `empty_at` exactly through all 8 turns (3 tests, ~3 s). That is exact enough: `FIELD_VERDICT_EPS` is 1e-5.
- What the view does NOT give: a way to **cut** the field in the new frame. There is no `CarriedField::simulate`.

## 2. The floor: a two-sided read exists, but only for an uncut floor

`field_floor::floor_at` reads the floor as the shell's lowest crossing on the column (a mesh plane, exact) and refuses by name (`CutFromBelow`) whenever any cut claim sits within one cell of the floor point - the 3x3x3 check from the review of #649. `read_column` turns that into an `Err`, so `column_body` **refuses the whole carry** for:
- a setup that drilled or slotted **through** the stock before the flip (`field_body::a_floor_a_cut_reached_refuses_the_carry_by_name`), and
- every neighbouring column within a cell of the hole wall.
Through-holes before a flip are the common re-clamp, so this refusal is the first thing step E has to lift.

**It can be lifted exactly, today, with no new record.** Every tool `Stock::simulate` builds spans the verdict world above its tip (`spanning_flank`: Flat/BullNose flank, the ball's shank). A solid that spans upward is **monotone on every vertical ray**: if it holds `(x, y, z)` it holds `(x, y, z')` for every `z' > z` in the world. So the material left in a column is ONE interval `[mesh floor, tool bottom]` or nothing: a cut from above can lower the top, never raise the floor, and it reaches the floor only by cutting through. Hence:
- `march` gives `Top(t)` -> material `[shell floor, t]`, the floor exact from the crossing (the claim nearby is a tool that passed close, not one that went below `t` here - a material centre proves it);
- `march` gives `NoMaterial` -> either cut through, or a sliver thinner than a cell with no centre inside it. The cut layer already records the answer: `cut_ups` of the cell whose centre is the highest one below the floor plane holds the ray's entry into the swept solid (`field_ray::vertical_entry`; closed-form for a flat floor, `flat_floor_entry`). `tool bottom = centre + u`; material iff `tool bottom >= floor` (the column engine's `t < f` empty law, same strictness).
- The law fails only for a solid that does NOT span the world above its tip: `Taper` (the field's cone is truncated at `r` - the "chimney" `backend.rs` already names), a bare `Ball`, a lathe sweep, a posed axis. The field marks itself (`bounded_cuts`) when such a sweep is subtracted, and keeps today's `CutFromBelow` refusal then. Never a guess.

This is the first slice (below). It completes step D's two-sided read for every upright program and changes no shipped verdict: the column engine is still the default and the field's down-march is untouched.

## 3. The mutation paths - what the holders actually do after a carry

| Holder | What it does to the carried body |
|---|---|
| `stock_sim_carry::walk` | `Held::Carried(body.carry(&turn)?)`, then `simulate(held.dex_mut(), ..)` for every later op; `clip_to_setup_stock(dex_mut)` lowers columns to the next setup's grid (box OR cylinder - `stock_grid`'s tops) |
| `rest/across::sweep` | `first_body -> carry -> simulate(&mut body.dex)` per segment, cached as `Arc<Body>` (`carried_cache`), its `dex` handed out as the rest grid |
| `rest::PriorPlan::simulate` | the same chain for verify's dive acquittal, returns a `Dexel` |
| `Held::Plain(Dexel)` | before the first carry; `first_body` turns it into a `Body` at the first carry |

So the field arm needs: **(a)** cuts in the NEW frame after a carry, flips included (`setup_carry::a_gouge_cut_before_the_flip_is_still_judged_after_it` cuts on both sides); **(b)** a clip by intersection (`Clip::Block`, #651 - a cylinder stock's clip is not a box and refuses by name on the field arm); **(c)** a `Body` read-back for the consumers that still take a `Dexel` (#587's motion masks, verify's prior, the display) - `column_body`, step D.

**(a) is the design question.** Two routes, both needing the same new primitive (an upward march reading a cut floor exactly):
- **(i) Cut through the view.** Map each move by `turn.unapply` into the field's frame. After a flip the tool axis is `-Z` there. `subtract_batch` accepts any axis (posed moves), but the two `+Z`-only closed forms are lost - `arc_sweeps` (true XY circle, #413; a flipped arc would ride chords and disagree with the column engine's exact arc) and `flat_floor_entry` (the exact flat floor; the search leaves the 1e-12 hair that broke the rest ladder's strict mask) - and `cut_ups` would need a recorded `cut_downs` twin for `-Z` sweeps. Three modules grow `+-Z` twins, each new verdict code to prove.
- **(ii) Bake the turn's signed permutation into the bricks, keep only the translation as the view.** The field's lattice is origin-locked (`cell_of(v) = floor(v / cell)`), and a signed permutation maps cell `i` to cell `i` or `-i-1` exactly - cell centres onto cell centres, "re-index, never re-sample", `Body::carry`'s own law on the bricks (`brick (b, slot) -> (-b-1, mirrored slot)`). Mesh facets and the analytic box transform exactly; the cost ledger is rebuilt (`region_of`). On a flip, each `cut_ups` record ("entry going up from the centre") becomes a `cut_downs` record ("entry going down"), so the swap IS the record: nothing new is computed at cut time and the hot path (`claim`) is untouched. Every later cut rides the shipped `+Z` code unchanged: arcs stay true arcs, the flat floor stays closed-form. The residual translation is applied to the moves (`from`, `to`, the arc centre - a translation keeps an arc's sense) and to the read-back's lattice.
- **Recommendation: (ii).** One new mechanical module (the re-index), one new march (`march_up`, the mirror of `march`/`refine` reading `cut_downs`), no twin of any cut-path closed form, no per-claim cost. The up-march also needs `refine` to read an uncut plane from the shell crossing rather than the cell boundary, so a flipped stock bottom that is not lattice-aligned reads exactly (the view read-back already does, through `floor_at`).

## 4. Performance

- The read-back costs one down-march per column of the new lattice (plus the up-march after (ii)), the same order as `deviate_field` - ~3 s for the 20x12 fixture through 8 turns in debug.
- The bake is O(allocated bricks x 512) once per carry, far under one `simulate` of a setup; the view's `unapply` per query is a few multiplies.
- Slice 1 adds no cost to a cut: the floor law reads records `claim` already keeps.
- `carried_cache` keeps `Arc<Body>` keyed on the chain; a field carry caches the same read-back, so the hit rate law (#321) is unchanged.

## 5. The agreement law

Three lanes, all heavy (`--ignored`) except the sim one:
1. `carry_engine_agreement` (sim, in quick): grows a through-slot and a floor-sliver fixture (slice 1), then a cut-after-flip fixture (E2c): the same block, slot from the top, flipped, slot from the new top, both engines agree per column on `empty_at`, top and floor to 1e-6.
2. An app-level twin of `stock_engine_agreement` once the holders are on the seam (#586): `walk` on both engines over the `setup_carry`, `rest_across_setups` and `carried_verify` fixtures, 0 findings within `FIELD_VERDICT_EPS` on the rest and gouge verdicts, top and floor; `floor_judged` equal; the carried `Deviation`s compared value for value.
3. `stock_engine_agreement` and `stock_backend_parity` stay as they are - the single-setup law.

## 6. Build order (each PR behaviour-neutral for the column engine, which stays the default)

- **E1 (this branch):** the field column's floor under a cut, read exactly by the monotone law; `CutFromBelow` kept only for bounded tools. `column_body` then carries through-holes and slivers.
- **E2a:** `SdfField::turned(&LatticeTurn) -> (SdfField, Point3)` - the bake, records swapped on a flip; pinned by invariance against the view.
- **E2b:** `march_up` + the mirrored column span, reading a baked flipped stock's cut floor exactly.
- **E2c:** `CarriedField::simulate(ops)` through the residual translation; the cut-after-flip agreement fixture.
- **E3 = #586:** `Held` over an engine-agnostic carried stock (`Carried::Column(Body) | Field(..)`) with `carry / clip / simulate / judge / body`, column default, byte-identical; the app agreement lane. Then #589 flips the default.

Considered and dropped are in `docs/decisions/637-carried-stock-field.md` on the branch. Sub-issues for E2a-c follow in the next comment.

Sub-issues for the build order above: #779 (E2a, the bake), #780 (E2b, the upward march and cut_downs), #781 (E2c, cuts through the carry). E3 is #586's own remaining work (the holders), then #589. E1 - the exact floor under a cut by the monotone law - lands on this branch (issue/637-carried-stock-field).

claimed: SKULL (Claude agent, mkinney fork) · 2026-11-12 05:10 UTC · worktree/branch issue/637-carried-stock-field · plan: answer the four design questions first (comment + decision file: transformed query frame vs re-sample, floor read, SDF-max clipping, agreement lane), then carry Stock through stock_sim_carry / rest / rest-across / priors with a heavy-lane agreement test against the column carry; Refs if only part lands

Design, phase 1 (SKULL worker, issue-worker-max, on upstream/main a6bd69d8 = v0.18.0 + #1032). Steps A-E2c shipped in v0.18.0 (#646, #649, #651, #656, #782, #784, #817, #831), so the field's side of a carry exists. Below: the four questions answered against that code, then the plan for what is left (the app holders, step E3). No shipped verdict or tolerance changes: the column engine stays the default.

**What was decided.**

1. **Representation: a transformed query frame, never a re-sample - and
   the bake is a re-index, not a re-sample either.** A signed distance is
   invariant under rigid motion, so the carried solid is the same field
   read through the turn (`CarriedField`). Under the eight lattice turns a
   vertical column of the new frame is a vertical column of the field's
   own, so a verdict column is one exact two-sided read (`column_span`).
   To cut after a carry the turn's signed permutation is moved into the
   bricks (`SdfField::turned`): the lattice is origin-locked, so cell
   centres land on cell centres and every stored value is copied. It is
   exact enough for the verdicts: the sim lane `carry_engine_agreement`
   holds tops and floors to 1e-6 per column through all eight turns, under
   `FIELD_VERDICT_EPS` (1e-5), and no verdict tolerance moves.
   One thing the app adds: the document's stock lattice starts at the
   stock's corner, not at a multiple of the cell. The field arm therefore
   builds its solid in the lattice's own frame (corner at the origin) and
   keeps the corner as the view's translation, so every verdict column
   sits on a field cell centre from the first cut on.
2. **The floor: the lower end of the column's one material interval.**
   A closed solid has no floor array; `column_span` reads `[floor, top]`
   from the shell crossings and the cut records (the monotone law for
   spanning tools, the up-march after a flip), and refuses by name where a
   bounded tool cut near the floor. A column cut through holds nothing.
   The column engine keeps the tool's own depth there (`top < floor`,
   both finite) and the verdict still convicts it; the read-back used to
   write "air" (`-inf`), which a verdict reads as "nothing to judge" - a
   false clear. Decided: **a cut-through column reads its top at the
   stock's own floor and its floor at the stock's own top** (both finite,
   `top < floor`): the column stays empty, and where the part stands the
   verdict convicts it from the top, and from below once the floor is
   judged. The field does not know how far below the stock's floor the
   tool travelled, so the gouge DEPTH there is the stock's, not the
   tool's: at least the part's full thickness, since the part lies inside
   the stock. The class (gouge) is the same as the column engine's.
3. **The clip is the column law as a solid, not a plain intersection.**
   The column clip lowers a column to the entered setup's stock top only
   where that stock's grid has a column; outside it what stands is left
   alone, and the floor is not touched. As a solid that is the carried
   body minus the half-infinite prism above the new stock's top over its
   footprint: `max(d_body, -d_prism)`. Max/min of signed distances keep
   the zero set exactly (they bound the distance, they do not equal it),
   and the verdicts read only membership along columns, so the clip is
   applied where the columns are read. A full intersection with the new
   block (`Clip::Block`, step C) would also delete what stands outside the
   new block and below its floor - less material than the column engine
   reports, the unsafe direction - so the holders do not use it. The
   footprint and tops are the entered setup's own stock grid, kept with
   the turns applied since, so a box and a cylinder clip alike and a later
   flip turns the ceiling into a floor bound.
4. **The agreement lane.** Three layers:
   - sim, quick lane: `carry_engine_agreement` (the read through every
     turn, cuts after a flip) and new `carried_stock` pins for the holder
     type (offset lattice, clip, cut-through read) on both engines.
   - app, heavy lane: `carried_engine_agreement` (`#[ignore]`, release):
     the scenarios of `setup_carry`, `rest_across_setups` and
     `carried_verify` built once and read on both engines - the program
     verdict column for column within `FIELD_VERDICT_EPS` with the same
     class, counts and aggregates; the incoming body's tops, floors,
     empties, volume and `floor_judged`; the rest grid; the bounds verify
     reads. Zero findings, printed whole before the suite fails.
   - the engine is picked per thread (`stock_sim::carry::with_engine`),
     so one process runs both; the existing carried suites can be run
     whole on the field arm with `CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE=field`.

**The holders.** camcraft-sim gains `CarriedStock` (`Column(Body)` |
`Field(FieldBody)`): build, carry, clip, simulate, and one read-back
(`body()`) onto the column body, so `deviate`, `display`, `volume` and
`bounds` stay the column carry's own code on both arms (step D's
decision, kept). `stock_sim_carry::Held`, `rest/across::sweep` and
`rest::PriorPlan` hold `Stock` / `CarriedStock` instead of `Dexel` /
`Body`. The column engine stays the default, so every shipped verdict,
golden and stamp is byte-identical; #589 flips the default.

**Why.** The rule for every choice: the field read never reports less
material than is there, and never turns a convicted column into "no
verdict". Reading back onto the column body keeps one verdict
implementation (the one the goldens already prove) instead of a second
two-sided verdict on the field.

**Considered and dropped.**
- *A field stock with the column's semi-infinite floor* (ten spans of
  phantom material below, clipped at read-back, as `Stock::block` does):
  it would keep the tool's depth below the stock, but after a flip every
  cut sweeps through the phantom above the part - the 35-40x cost noted
  on #586. A closed solid costs the same both ways up.
- *`Clip::Block` for the app clip*: drops material outside the new block
  (above).
- *A cylinder stock on the field arm from its mesh*: the mesh is an
  inscribed polygon, so rim columns would hold less than the column
  engine's disc. Refused by name on the field arm for now
  (`FIELD_CARRY_SHAPE_REFUSAL`); the column arm is unchanged.
- *Passing the engine as a parameter through every rest and job call*:
  some twenty signatures for a switch #589 removes again.

**Cost to change later.** The cut-through read is one function
(`FieldBody::body`); a field that records the tool's depth below the
stock could replace it without touching the holders. The engine switch
is one thread-local and one environment read in `stock_sim_carry`.

**Build, this branch (`issue/637-carried-stock-field`):** `CarriedStock` in camcraft-sim, the holders in `stock_sim_carry` / `rest` / `rest/across` onto it, the heavy lane `carried_engine_agreement`. The same text is in `docs/decisions/637-carried-stock-holders.md` on the branch.
